raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Under DSpark decode, the three draft stages compute the mixing statistics of their six mHC boundaries with the Triton split-K kernel (`hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn`) at every batch, while the target layers run DeepGEMM's `tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm` from 128 rows. Two reasons: the DSpark model never calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache`, so its stages have no TF32 weight parts, and `_mix_stats_impl` keeps the DeepGEMM path off under 128 rows on SM100 (SM90 uses it from 32).

Measured on GB300 (DEP16 decode, DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, 128K contexts, torch profiler, kernel durations):

| Draft rows (= requests per rank) | `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel`, 6 launches | `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel`, 6 launches | Per cycle |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 6 x 23.8 us | 6 x 9.0 us | 0.197 ms |
| 64 | 6 x 42.2 us | 6 x 9.1 us | 0.307 ms |
| 256 | 6 x 150 us | 6 x 10.5 us | 0.963 ms |

In the same traces the target's unfused boundaries run `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_impl` at 7.4-7.9 us per launch (160 and 320 rows) plus a 16-slice reduce of 7.8 us: about 23 us per boundary against 52 us on the Triton path at 64 rows. The 128-row floor is not a kernel requirement: DeepGEMM's SM100 kernel uses `block_m = 64` with a grid of `num_splits x ceil_div(m, 64)` and no assertion on M.

## Modifications

- `DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark.post_load_weights` calls `refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache` on each stage, which builds the TF32 parts of the 24 x 20,480 mixing weights (24 MB per GPU for three stages).
- `_mix_stats_impl`: the row floor for the TF32 parts becomes 32 on SM100 as on SM90 (`x_flat.shape[0] >= 32` replaces `>= 128 or hopper_medium`, which already meant 32 on SM90). Batch-invariant mode and rows under 32 are unchanged.

Expected: about 0.17 ms less per decode cycle at 64 requests per rank (22.6 ms cycle), 0.06 ms at 32.

## Accuracy Tests

The draft's statistics move from the Triton tf32x3 kernel to the two-part TF32 split the target already runs at 128 rows and above. Accept length from the A/B decode logs will be posted here; GSM8K at native acceptance on request.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The A/B at 64 requests per rank (same recipe, base main 49766a74f9 against this branch) is running; the six draft launches and the log cycle will be posted here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

nodes.body:
🚀 `4-gpu-gb300` (1 test): ✅ [View workflow run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39347151049) <!--rrt:0:done-->
```
cd test/ && python3 registered/e2e/models/test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300_tp4ep4.py
```

🚀 `1-gpu-h100` (1 test): ✅ [View workflow run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39347163356) <!--rrt:1:done-->
```
cd test/ && python3 registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_kernels.py
```

A/B on GB300, DEP16 decode (DP attention 16, EP 16), DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash, 128K-token random-id prompts, Mega-mHC on, decode graph 64, torch profiler over 20 steps on all 16 ranks, base main `49766a74f9` vs this branch at `0a168b0ec9`. Both arms ran 61 requests per rank (one draft row each).

Draft step, the six mHC boundaries' statistics, median over ranks:

| Arm | Launches | Per decode cycle |
|---|---|---:|
| base (Triton split-K) | `_hc_mix_stats_partial_kernel` 6 x 42 us, `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel` 6 x 9 us | 0.309 ms |
| branch (TF32) | `sm100_tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm_impl` 12 x 6.8 us, `_hc_mix_reduce_sinkhorn_kernel` 6 x 7.6 us | 0.126 ms |

Summed kernel time per draft step 2.53 to 2.28 ms; verify step unchanged (20.33 vs 20.34 ms outside the first routed-MoE launch). Accept length from the decode log 3.50-3.51 on the branch, 3.52 on the base. The end-to-end cycle from the log (`#running-req x accept len / gen throughput`) differs by 0.0-0.3 ms between the arms, inside the spread of one window, so the cycle gain is not resolved by this measurement; the kernel-level saving is 0.18 ms per cycle at 61 rows (0.8% of a 22.3 ms cycle).

One thing I could not explain: with this branch the engine admitted 61-62 requests per rank with the rest waiting where the base admitted 64 on the same recipe, on two different node sets; the token pool is 24,064 tokens smaller (the TF32 parts) and sat at 7% usage. If anyone knows a pool or budget that the draft model's parameter size feeds into, I would like to hear it.

files.patch:
@@ -1062,6 +1062,11 @@ def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> None:
         self._assert_confidence_head_loaded(
             params_dict=params_dict, loaded_params=loaded_params
         )
+        self.post_load_weights()
+
+    def post_load_weights(self, is_nextn=False, weight_names=None):
+        for stage in self.stages:
+            stage.refresh_mhc_norm_weight_cache()
 
     def _assert_confidence_head_loaded(
         self, *, params_dict: dict, loaded_params: set

@@ -278,7 +278,7 @@ def _mix_stats_impl(hc: HcSubLayer, x: torch.Tensor) -> HcTriplet:
     hopper_medium = get_platform().is_sm90 and 32 <= x_flat.shape[0] < 4096
     if (
         x.is_cuda
-        and (x_flat.shape[0] >= 128 or hopper_medium)
+        and x_flat.shape[0] >= 32
         and x_flat.is_contiguous()
         and (get_platform().is_sm100 or get_platform().is_sm90)
         and envs.SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM.get()
